name: Can kitchen storage be redesigned for someone with limited reach or mobility?

mainEntity.name: Can kitchen storage be redesigned for someone with limited reach or mobility?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen remodel can be planned around accessibility needs by reducing reach, improving pull-out access, and placing controls and daily items within comfortable ranges. The exact design should reflect the user’s mobility, reach, balance, and whether assistance is needed. Context: Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate household-specific use requirements into layout and cabinet planning rather than applying one universal setup. Wider clearances or altered work surfaces may affect the footprint and cost. Key factors: reach range; seated versus standing use; drawer force; appliance controls; turning space. Practical guidance: Describe the user’s actual movements and difficult tasks during the consultation. Bring measurements for mobility equipment if relevant. Review cabinet elevations and open-door clearances before construction so the design is tested against real use.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, planning can emphasize reachable storage, pull-outs, easier hardware, suitable work heights, and clearer movement paths. The design should reflect the person’s actual reach and mobility needs, including equipment dimensions when relevant.
